resale_co.name: Residential Owner Certificate (Ownership Certificate, Town Code Chapter 148 "Certificates of Occupancy")
resale_co.issued_by: Town of West New York Code Enforcement / Building Department (Director of Public Affairs or designee, or the Construction Code Official), with a Fire Prevention Residential Ownership Review
requirements: Boilers/furnaces: a full fire-rated ceiling or a sprinkler installed on the code water line
All final inspections on any permits finalized
Egress free and clear; inspector must have entry to all areas of the property
Exit doors free of padlocks and key locks; exit signs and emergency lighting working where present
Fire extinguisher within ten feet of any kitchen, properly mounted and readily accessible
Handrails on all stairs with 3 or more risers plus landings, interior and exterior
No keyed locks on any interior doors
Smoke detectors and carbon monoxide alarms
No trash or rubbish accumulation inside or outside
No outstanding building code or property maintenance violations
Windows operable, no broken or cracked glass

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Residential Owner Certificate application (anticipated closing date, present owner and purchasers; LLCs must name the manager or principal). The purchaser signs the Certification/Affidavit on page 2 in front of a notary, and the applicant meets with the Fire Prevention office for the Fire Prevention Residential Ownership Review on page 3. File with the Code Enforcement / Building Department, Municipal Building, 428-60th Street, Office No. 27, with the fee payable to Town of West New York.

evidence.quote: It shall henceforth be unlawful for any owner or prospective purchaser of real property to sell, convey, delivery or transfer, and for any purchaser to purchase, take title or possession of, any residential building or premises until an ownership certificate, to the effect that such residential building or premise complies with and conforms to the provisions of this article, shall have been issued by the Director of the Department of Public Affairs or his designee.
WHEREAS, the Town seeks to clarify that an ownership certificate is required for the sale of residential, commercial, mixed use and vacant properties.

then the Director of the Department of Public Affairs or his designee may issue a nonrenewable temporary ownership certificate for a period not in excess of six months from the date of conveyance or transfer of possession.
The responsibility and liability for obtaining or not obtaining the Ownership Certificate is both with the property owner and the prospective purchaser.

resale_co.notes: Town Code Chapter 148 (as replaced by Ordinance #6/16, 2016) makes it unlawful to sell or to take title to a residential building until an ownership certificate is issued after inspection; both seller and buyer are responsible. For "as is" sales a nonrenewable temporary certificate of up to six months can be issued if violations will not be fixed before closing. Current fees come from the December 2025 Residential Owner Certificate application (scan read visually; three to ten unit dwelling $250, each unit over ten $50). The $50 reinspection fee on the 2025 form is higher than the $25 failed-inspection fee in the 2016 fee ordinance (#5/16); the form is newer. The live westnewyorknj.org site shows a bot check, so pages and files are cited from Internet Archive copies (originals: https://www.westnewyorknj.org/departments/building-department/, the 2025/12 application in application_url, https://www.westnewyorknj.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/ord616.pdf and ord516.pdf). The 2025 form header shows the Construction Official office number as 201.295.5170; the department page gives his line as 201-295-5173. Separate certificates exist for residential tenants (rental), commercial, mixed use and vacant land.

requirements: Smoke detectors must be 10-year sealed by the manufacturer (since January 1, 2019); AC powered or interconnected alarms in homes after January 1977 must be kept working

The 2025 Town forms still require a portable fire extinguisher: minimum 2A:10B:C, no more than 10 pounds, within 10 feet of the kitchen in the exit path, top no more than 5 feet above the floor, mounted on the maker's bracket, with the owner's manual, serviced and tagged by a DFS-certified contractor within 12 months or a recent purchase receipt
Smoke detector certificates are valid for six months; if the change of occupant does not happen within 6 months a new application is needed
A notarized application and certification in lieu of inspection is offered; the Fire Prevention Bureau may do a follow-up inspection within 12 months

fire_cert.notes: West New York is registry code S*: the State enforces the fire code only in life hazard uses and the local agency enforces everything else, so the Town Office of Fire Prevention issues the resale smoke/CO certificate (the DCA state towns list does not mark West New York "SC"). The state directory lists Louis Kilmer as Fire Official for the State LEA and "West New York Town Fire Prev", (201) 295-5220 for smoke detector compliance. The fee is a flat $150 per the 2025 form, which cites Ordinance 1/19 amending Chapter 198 (the form text still mentions tiers based on time before the change of occupant, but lists only the one $150 amount). The form names the certificate "CSDCMAC" (Certificate of Smoke Detector and Carbon Monoxide Alarm Compliance). Fire Official contact: the June 2026 page lists Robert Torres Jr. at 201-295-5221 and rtorres@westnewyorknj.org; the 2025 form prints O. 201.295.5220 (office line). Fire suppression is by North Hudson Regional Fire & Rescue.

other_items.label: Purchaser affidavit
other_items.detail: The purchaser must sign a notarized Certification/Affidavit stating the number of dwelling units and agreeing to follow the Hotel and Multiple Dwelling Law and local codes if units change.

other_items.label: Fire Prevention Residential Ownership Review
other_items.detail: The applicant meets with the WNY Fire Prevention office, which marks whether the property does or does not require approvals from that office for the title transfer.

other_items.label: Temporary certificate for as-is sales
other_items.detail: If violations will not be corrected before closing, a nonrenewable temporary ownership certificate of up to six months may be issued; the as-is agreement must be attached and the application signed by seller and buyer.
